Wike made the declaration on Wednesday during an interaction with political stakeholders in Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC), where speakers from both parties credited his leadership with fostering political cooperation and promoting infrastructure development across the territory. The minister said he had been assigned the responsibility of coordinating support for Tinubu in Rivers State and the FCT, expressing confidence that both would vote for the president in 2027. “I was given two assignments: to coordinate for Rivers State, to ensure Rivers State is given to Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and to ensure the FCT is delivered to Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu. To the glory of God, FCT is for Tinubu, Rivers is for Tinubu,” he said. He urged residents to support the president, arguing that the administration’s record in infrastructure, governance and political inclusion provided a basis for its re-election campaign. Wike said the Tinubu administration had addressed longstanding concerns over the representation of FCT indigenes in government, particularly their career progression in the civil service. According to him, indigenous workers previously faced barriers to attaining senior positions, including permanent secretary and Head of Service. “Before, you could not become a permanent secretary in the FCT. Nobody could become a head of service in the FCT. There was frustration; you could not get to the highest level of your career,” he said. He added that the situation had improved with the appointment of permanent secretaries, the emergence of a Head of Service and the establishment of a Civil Service Commission to oversee employment matters in the territory. The minister also cited administrative structures for women and youths as evidence of what he described as inclusive governance. “That is inclusivity. Women can carry their burden to the secretariat, youths can carry their burden to the secretariat, and the government will have to listen to them,” he said. On infrastructure, Wike said his administration had extended development to the six area councils through consultations with traditional rulers, women, youths and other community stakeholders. He said the consultations helped identify priority projects, including roads, police stations and other essential facilities, which the administration had been addressing. “Today, the six area councils can boast of roads going to the various areas. It was not like that before. Area councils did not feel the impact of government,” he said. Wike disclosed that 12 police stations with residential quarters had been constructed to strengthen security across the FCT. He also promised to complete and commission additional infrastructure projects, including roads, in the coming months. He said the administration would base its campaign on projects delivered and those still being executed, rather than relying solely on political rhetoric. “While other people are preparing for election, we are not going to talk about election; we are going to talk about commissioning of projects. “Our campaign is our project. Our campaign is to tell you what we have done. Our campaign is, if you give us the support, we will do more,” he said. Acknowledging that the Tinubu administration had yet to resolve all the country’s economic challenges, Wike maintained that it had made significant progress within its first three years. “We cannot say that this government has solved every problem. No. But within three years, they have solved a lot of problems,” he said. He defended the administration’s economic reforms, including the removal of fuel subsidy, arguing that difficult decisions were necessary to address the country’s economic challenges. The minister urged women, youths, traditional rulers, community leaders, and political stakeholders to mobilise support for Tinubu, stressing that the outcome of the 2027 election would depend on voter turnout. He also cautioned supporters against assuming that the president’s re-election was guaranteed, urging political leaders to engage residents directly and address their concerns. The APC and PDP leadership in AMAC expressed support for Tinubu’s re-election and commended Wike for bringing members of the two parties together despite their longstanding political differences. The APC Chairman in the FCT, Tanko Yamawo, said the political cooperation had helped ease tensions that previously divided families and communities during election periods. “Before now, when you are approaching election, some of us don’t talk to our own brothers because they are in the other party. “But today, we are sitting in the same room, both APC and PDP, because somebody has changed the narrative of politics,” he said. He said the collaboration was driven by a shared interest in FCT development, adding that the parties were working together despite their different political affiliations. “Today we are in partnership with PDP for the progress of the people of FCT,” he said. Yamawo also commended Tinubu for appointing an FCT indigene as a minister, describing it as a longstanding demand of the territory’s indigenous population. “These are things we have gone on the street for years protesting, and this time it was given to us without protest,” he said. He further cited infrastructure projects and the integration of indigenous communities, including Gishiri and Gwarinpa, as reasons for his support for the administration. Describing Wike as an experienced political leader capable of coordinating the campaign in the territory, Yamawo expressed confidence in his leadership. “I have boarded the plane, and I will be comfortable, and I will be sleeping with my two eyes closed, as APC has given us Barrister Nyesom Wike as coordinator of our campaign in FCT,” he said. Similarly, the FCT Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chairman, Ismaila Dogara Yenche, said the relationship between the two parties had shifted from hostility to cooperation. “It used to be cat and rat. They could not see themselves in the daytime or in the midnight. But today, rat and cat are eating from the same plate,” Yenche said. He attributed the development to Wike’s emphasis on infrastructure and political inclusion, arguing that cooperation would serve the interests of FCT residents better than persistent partisan divisions. “Instead of us having brothers within ourselves, we should follow that development,” he said. Yenche also praised the Tinubu administration for what he described as improved representation of FCT indigenes in national affairs, saying Wike had created opportunities for them to participate more actively in governance. He urged political leaders, traditional rulers and residents to support the administration’s development agenda, expressing confidence that the emerging cooperation would translate into votes for Tinubu in 2027. “What reason do we have? You say that we are not going to support Mr President. Do we have a reason? No! We have no reason,” he said. Also speaking, the chairman of the Igbo Traditional Rulers Council in the FCT and President-General of the Association of Eze Ndigbo in the 19 Northern States and the FCT, Eze Dr Uche Egenti, MON, commended Wike for infrastructure development across the territory. Egenti said the projects had benefited residents irrespective of their political, religious or ethnic backgrounds, urging the FCT Administration to sustain the pace of development. “Irrespective of political party, irrespective of religious inclination and tribal leaning, everybody is enjoying your infrastructural revolution,” he said. He expressed appreciation for the transformation underway in Abuja, adding that indigenous residents had reason to acknowledge the administration’s efforts. “The indigenous residents of Abuja will always have kind words for you for what you are doing, what you have done and what you are doing,” he said. Egenti also commended Tinubu and prayed for the president’s good health and success, while urging Wike to continue implementing projects that improve residents’ welfare. “We want to say, please keep on doing the good work you are doing,” he said. The traditional ruler further praised the AMAC leadership for maintaining an open relationship with stakeholders and making itself accessible to community representatives.
